figures.message: A noisy label that the out-of-fold model disagrees with is usually flipped, so dropping those samples wins back much of the accuracy noise costs (most on digits), beats an untuned MLP, and costs nothing measurable on clean labels.
figures.layout: One row, three panels, widths about 30/45/25 percent, lowercase panel letters (a), (b), (c), no titles inside panels, sans-serif regular, legends above or beside the axes and never over data. (a) 'Does disagreement find flips?': x groups are digits 20%, digits 40%, breast cancer 20%, breast cancer 40%; two bars per group, precision (share of drops truly flipped) in #4E2A84 and recall (share of flipped labels dropped) in #B6ACD1; y: percent, 0 to 100; dashed gray line at 50% labeled 'half of drops'; error bars are sd over 5 seeds on precision bars. (b) 'Does dropping them help?': two small line subplots side by side (digits, breast cancer), x: label noise 0, 20, 40%, y: test accuracy (%); lines for logistic regression (muted teal), MLP (muted orange-brown) and the filter (#4E2A84, thicker, labeled 'ours'); shaded bands or error bars are sd over 5 seeds; a thin gray dashed horizontal line marks logistic regression on clean labels, and a light lavender #F1EEF7 bracket at 40% marks the gap between noisy logistic regression and clean level, with the filter inside it. (c) 'What does it cost when labels are clean?': two bars (digits, breast cancer) of filter minus logistic regression at 0% noise in points, #4E2A84, with 95% paired-interval error bars crossing zero, zero line in gray; beside them two light purple bars with the share (%) of clean training samples dropped, on a second small axis.
figures.error_bars: Panel a and b: sd over 5 seeds (no sd recipe exists for recall, so recall bars have no error bars). Panel c: 95% interval of the paired difference over 5 seeds. Per-seed dots are omitted because no recipe stores per-seed values.
figures.caption_draft: Out-of-fold disagreement finds flipped labels, and dropping those samples recovers much of the accuracy that label noise costs a linear model. (a) Share of dropped samples that were truly flipped (precision, purple) and share of flipped labels that were dropped (recall, light purple) at 20% and 40% symmetric noise; error bars are sd over 5 seeds, and the dashed line marks 50%. Most drops are flips and most flips are dropped. (b) Test accuracy against noise rate for logistic regression, an untuned MLP, and our filter (purple); the gray line is logistic regression on clean labels. The filter closes much of the gap on digits, and the MLP falls fastest. (c) On clean labels the paired accuracy change of the filter against logistic regression (95% interval, 5 seeds) includes zero, at the price of dropping a few percent of clean samples.

figures.message: The filter is four steps: split the noisy training set into folds, predict each sample with a model that never saw it, drop the samples whose prediction disagrees with the label, and refit on the rest.
figures.layout: Four flat pastel rounded panels on a lavender #F1EEF7 background, arranged in a 2 by 2 grid read left to right then down (column width), each marked by a small numbered circle and a plain regular-weight title, joined by thick rounded arrows. 1 'Noisy labels': a small grid of sample tiles with colored class tags, a few tags in red-orange to show flips. 2 'Predict out of fold': the grid cut into five strips, a purple network card trained on four strips with an arrow to the held-out fifth strip. 3 'Drop disagreements': tiles whose predicted class differs from the tag are crossed out. 4 'Refit': a purple network card trained on the kept tiles, with a check icon. Icons come from one shared set drawn in TikZ, no gradients, no equations, labels of one to three words.
figures.caption_draft: Out-of-fold filtering in four steps. (1) The training labels contain flips. (2) Logistic regression is fit with K-fold cross-validation, so each sample is predicted by a model that did not see it. (3) Every sample whose out-of-fold prediction disagrees with its given label is dropped. (4) Logistic regression is refit on the kept samples. The filter uses no clean validation set and no estimate of the noise rate; we use K = 5.
